title: Ndolé with Beef, Prawns and Peanuts (Afro Fusion style)
author: martymadeitproductions (martymadeit.com), crediting afrofusionbrands.com
desc: Bone-in beef simmered with onion and seasoning, peanuts blended with ginger, celery, leek and garlic, bitter leaf cooked to a thick paste, and 30 prawns fried with garlic and onion as the topping.
longDesc: This printing credits an original at afrofusionbrands.com. Beef with bones is simmered with half an onion, seasoning, bouillon and salt over medium heat until tender. Parboiled fresh peanuts are blended with ginger, onion, habanero, leek, celery and three garlic cloves; oil is heated, a diced onion sautéed, and the beef and peanut paste added and simmered 25 minutes, stirring every 5 to 10 minutes so it does not scorch. Crayfish and the bitter leaf go in and cook 10 to 15 minutes until a thick paste forms. The garnish is 30 prawns fried about 3 minutes with minced garlic until pink, then a minced onion for 3 to 5 minutes until translucent, spooned over about 5 minutes before serving. Served with boiled sweet plantain or corn fufu.
ingredients: 1.5 lbs beef with bones, cut into pieces
4 cups large yellow onions, finely chopped or sliced (divided; reserve 1 for garnish)
2 tablespoons Afro Fusion All Purpose Seasoning (brand mix — contents not printed)
3 cups fresh peanuts, de-pulped and parboiled 5 minutes
1/2 cup leeks, scallions or green onions
1/2 cup peanut oil (divided), or to taste
3 cups beef stock (listed; no step uses it)
steps: Simmer the beef with half an onion, the seasoning, bouillon and salt over medium heat until tender. (The time is not printed.)
Blend the peanuts with the ginger, half an onion, habanero, leek, celery and 3 garlic cloves.
Heat the oil, sauté one diced onion, then add the beef and the peanut paste. Simmer 25 minutes, stirring every 5 to 10 minutes so it does not scorch.
Adjust salt and bouillon and stir in the crayfish. Add the bitter leaf and cook 10 to 15 minutes until it forms a thick paste.
Heat 3 tablespoons of oil and fry the prawns with 3 minced garlic cloves for about 3 minutes, until pink. Add one minced onion and cook 3 to 5 minutes, until translucent.
Spoon the garnish over the ndolé about 5 minutes before serving.
chefTips: Printed cues: ‘until tender’ (beef), ‘thick paste’ (bitter leaf), ‘until pink’ (prawns), ‘until translucent’ (onion).
Stir every 5 to 10 minutes during the 25-minute simmer.
The seasoning blend is a brand product; its contents are not printed, so substitute your own seasoning knowingly.
commonMistakes: Looking for where the 3 cups of beef stock go — the method never uses them.
Adding the garnish too early; the page spoons it on about 5 minutes before serving.
Skipping bitter leaf preparation: the page gives none (ABSENT).
healthBenefits: Beef, prawns and peanuts give protein; bitter leaf adds greens.
culturalNote: The page calls ndolé one of the national dishes of Cameroon and a staple in West Africa, and credits an original at afrofusionbrands.com. The byline is a production handle, not a personal name.
